issues.legal_issue: An allotment based on deemed vacancy cannot be made without first giving the landlord or tenant an opportunity to contest whether the conditions for deemed vacancy exist.
material_facts: The building was declared to be in deemed vacancy after an inspection conducted in the landlord’s absence.
The landlord sought time to file an objection after receiving notice, but the allotment was made the following day without giving him an opportunity to present his objection or submissions.
issues.conclusion: The allotment authority was required to hear the landlord before making an allotment based on deemed vacancy; the allotment made without that opportunity was a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 16(1) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act, 1972 makes it mandatory to give the landlord or tenant an opportunity to show that Section 12(4) does not apply before making an allotment order. Rule 8(2) requires an opportunity to object or make submissions. These requirements also reflect the principle of audi alteram partem.

predicates.deemed_vacancy_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding seeks an allotment on the basis that the building is deemed vacant.
predicates.landlord_or_tenant_not_given_opportunity: The landlord or tenant was not given an opportunity to show that the circumstances supporting deemed vacancy did not exist.

issues.definition: When an allotment proceeding is based on deemed vacancy and the landlord or tenant is not given an opportunity to contest that vacancy, the allotment order is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An allotment cannot be made without serving the landlord notice of the date on which allotment will be considered, so that the landlord can seek release of the building.
material_facts: The allotment authority did not serve the landlord with the notice required to inform him of the date on which the question of allotment would be considered.
The landlord was therefore not given the opportunity at that stage to seek release of the building for a qualifying purpose.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was entitled to notice of the date fixed for considering allotment, and the allotment order made without that notice and the resulting opportunity was a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 9(3) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Rules, 1972 requires notice to the landlord of the date fixed for considering allotment. In response, the landlord may seek release under Section 16(1)(b) for the purposes provided in Section 16(2). The allotment authority performs a quasi-judicial function and must observe natural justice.

predicates.building_allotment_proceeding: The authority is considering whether to allot a building that is vacant or treated as vacant.
predicates.landlord_not_served_notice_of_allotment_: The landlord was not served notice of the date on which the authority would consider allotment.

issues.definition: When a building-allotment proceeding takes place without service on the landlord of notice of the allotment-consideration date, the resulting allotment order is invalid.
